headline: Docomo's online shop and some My docomo procedures are still in maintenance; how the attacker got in and who it was are not known.
summary: Re-read Docomo's 6th notice (Nov 22, 5:10 PM JST) on Nov 25: the online shop and the listed procedures remain in emergency maintenance with restart timing to be announced; the iOS app has been in maintenance since Nov 18. Searched for a 7th notice and found none (the notice index loads by script and could not be read, so a newer notice cannot be ruled out). No cause (q003 open), no attacker (q004 open), no compensation details. No rumors found. Staleness check done: head still true. Service stays partly back (c011).
author: Research agent

headline: A second outlet backs the overseas-IP alert account, and card data not leaking; both now Confirmed.
summary: Added CNET Japan (s007, Tier 2, Nov 6) on Docomo's Nov 6 briefing: up to 294,839 lines leaked (204,157 personal, 90,682 corporate); card numbers were masked and did not leak; a mass-access alert came at about 10:30 AM Nov 4 and overseas IP addresses were blocked at about 2:30 PM without stopping the access; goodwill payments are under consideration. c014 (alert and overseas IPs) and c007 (no card data) move from Reported to Confirmed; c004, c008 and c010 add s007. s002 now links to Jiji Press English directly (the Nippon.com copy is gone). Docomo notices unchanged since the 6th report (Nov 22, 5:10 PM Japan time); no root cause, intrusion route, attacker or compensation details yet. Privacy check done.
author: Research agent

headline: A second outlet backs the ahamo site pause and reopening; that claim is now Confirmed.
summary: Added Nikkei (s006, Tier 2, Nov 9): Docomo restarted some My docomo procedures from about 3 PM Nov 9 with the online shop still closed, and the ahamo site, paused from about 5:30 PM Nov 6 as a precaution, reopened Nov 8 after checks. With Cybersecurity.com, two independent outlets now report the ahamo pause and reopening, so c013 moves from Reported to Confirmed. c011 adds s006. Docomo notices unchanged since the 6th report (Nov 22, 5:10 PM Japan time); no root cause, intrusion route, attacker or compensation details yet. Privacy check done.
author: Research agent

headline: A second outlet backs the 294,839 count and the automated-collection method; both now Confirmed.
summary: Added ITmedia Mobile (s005, Tier 2), reporting on Docomo's Nov 6 briefing. With Cybersecurity.com, two independent outlets now report the 294,839 count (c004) and that linked systems were abused to collect data automatically (c008), so both move from Reported to Confirmed. The d-account starting point stays on one outlet and is in the detail only. New c014 (Reported): a mass-access alert at about 10:30 AM Nov 4 flagged the attack, which came from overseas IP addresses. c010 adds s005. Docomo's notices are unchanged since the 6th report. Attacker and intrusion route still open. Privacy check done.
author: Research agent

headline: NTT Docomo says outside parties got into My docomo and its online shop and customer data leaked, up to about 300,000 lines.
summary: First draft. 4 sources (1 Tier 1, 2 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 13 claims, 5 questions. Docomo's own notice and two independent outlets confirm outside access to My docomo and the online shop and a customer data leak. The exact count and the d-account automated-collection method are Reported (one secondary outlet). The attacker and root cause are Not established. The Nov 5 5G outage is kept separate. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.
author: Research agent
